title: What Is an Agentic CDP? | Hightouch
summary: An agentic CDP uses AI agents to find, rank, and act on marketing opportunities in your customer data. Learn how it differs from traditional and composable CDPs.
body_markdown:
Plenty of marketers use their CDP the same way: they log in, build the audience they have in mind, launch the campaign they planned, and log out. The CDP makes that work faster and more accurately. The thinking still happens somewhere else: in a spreadsheet, a ticket to the analytics team, or a planning meeting.


That's been true for about a decade. CDPs added AI features, scoring models, and dashboards, and they still mostly carry out ideas that marketers bring to them.


An agentic CDP changes where the ideas come from. It can look at your data, notice something worth doing, and bring it to you with the evidence and a draft of the work.


## What is an agentic CDP?


An agentic CDP is a customer data platform that uses AI agents to analyze customer and campaign data, find and prioritize marketing opportunities, and help marketers act on them by building audiences, journeys, and reports. A traditional CDP carries out the plan a marketer brings to it. An agentic CDP helps come up with the plan.


In practice, that changes three things about what the CDP does:


- **It investigates the data.** Agents dig into customer behavior, campaign results, and channel performance to explain what's happening, instead of only storing and syncing data.
- **It brings ideas to you.** Agents can work toward goals you set and surface opportunities you didn't think to ask about.
- **It moves into the next step.** A finding can become an audience, a draft journey, or a recurring report without a new request to another team.


The word "agentic" matters because an agent does more than answer. It takes a goal, decides what to look at, works through several steps, and checks what it found.


## Conversations around your data don’t make a CDP agentic


Conversational AI (chat boxes similar to Chat GPT) is now standard in many CDPs and AI marketing tools. You type a question and get an answer back. That's useful, and we offer it too. If you ask "What were my top-selling products last month?" and the chat can see the right data, you'll get a good answer.


The trouble starts with bigger questions like "How can I grow subscription sales?" Chat tools tend to struggle with those for three reasons:


- They only see the data inside the platform they live in, so they miss campaigns, channels, and business priorities that live somewhere else.
- They're built to answer fast, so they grab the first idea that sounds right instead of comparing several.
- They lose track during long, open-ended investigations and get less reliable as they take in more information.


A chat box answers the question you already knew to ask. In marketing, the hard part is often figuring out which question to ask.


## What makes a CDP agentic


A CDP is agentic when its agents can do the digging and hand you something you can act on. Here's what that takes.


**It understands marketing, not just tables.** The agents work with the same things marketers do: audiences, journeys, campaigns, channels, conversion, retention, lifetime value (LTV), and churn. They know to judge an awareness campaign differently from a conversion campaign, and they check historical baselines before calling something a trend.


**It sees more than customer data.** Good recommendations need campaign results from ad and email platforms, business rules, goals, and creative performance, alongside the customer data in your warehouse.


**It works in the background toward your goals.** You tell it what you're trying to drive, like more repeat purchases or a stronger product launch, and agents keep looking for ways to get there.


**It ranks what it finds.** Ten ideas in no particular order give you more work, not less. An agentic CDP sorts opportunities by how many customers they could reach, what the outcome is worth, and how likely the idea is to work.


**It checks its own work.** The agents test each finding against the data before showing it to you and throw out anything the data can't support.


**It leads into action.** You can turn a finding into an audience, draft a journey, or schedule a report from the same place you found it.


**It remembers.** The agents save what they learn about your audiences, journeys, and campaigns, so the next recommendation builds on the last one.


### The hard part is knowing which ideas are worthwhile


AI can come up with ideas all day. The hard part is coming up with ideas worth a marketer's time, and that's the best way to tell an agentic CDP from one that offers suggestions.


If an agent surfaces 30 "opportunities" a day with no sense of impact, mistakes normal seasonal swings for real changes in customer behavior, or suggests discounts on premium products that you’d never put on sale, those insights aren’t going to deliver value.


## Traditional CDP vs. composable CDP vs. agentic CDP


An agentic CDP builds on the composable CDP rather than replacing it. The composable approach moved audiences, journeys, and activation onto the data warehouse, and that's what gives agents direct access to a company's richest customer and business data.


**Traditional CDP** **Composable CDP** **Agentic CDP**


**Where the data lives** Copied into the vendor's platform Stays in your warehouse Stays in your warehouse, plus connections to channels and business context


**Main job** Build audiences and sync them Build audiences and journeys on warehouse data Find opportunities, recommend next steps, and build what's needed to act


**Who has the ideas** The marketer The marketer The marketer and the agents


**How you work with it** Set up rules and workflows Set up models, audiences, and journeys Ask in plain language, set goals, and review recommendations


**What you get** Audiences and synced data Audiences, journeys, and synced data Ranked opportunities, evidence, audiences, draft journeys, and reports


**Marketer's role** Decide what to build Decide what to build, with more control Set goals, weigh opportunities, and approve what ships


## Agentic CDP vs. an AI analytics tool


Data teams often ask a fair question: why not use the AI tools already running on the warehouse, or a general AI assistant?


Those tools are good at answering questions about data, and an agentic CDP can use them. Our agents can tap into tools like Snowflake Cortex, Databricks Genie, Looker, and Omni. The difference is everything that happens around the answer. An agentic CDP connects to the ad and lifecycle platforms where your campaigns run, thinks in marketing terms, ranks and checks what it finds, and turns the finding into an audience or journey. You get a recommendation about what to do next and the start of the work, on top of the answer.


## What an agentic CDP looks like in practice


The three examples below are examples of what an agentic CDP workflow might look like. Each one follows the same loop: a goal, an investigation, evidence, a recommendation, an action, and a way to measure it.


### Paid media: spend efficiency is slipping


- **Goal:** Get paid social efficiency back on track.
- **Investigation:** The agent compares spend, conversions, and creative results across channels over the last several weeks.
- **Evidence:** A handful of ads that ran for weeks show falling click-through rates with the same audiences, a common sign of creative fatigue.
- **Recommendation:** Shift budget toward newer creative and refresh the tired concepts.
- **Action:** The team reviews the recommendation and hands the refresh to their creative workflow.
- **Measurement:** A scheduled weekly report tracks efficiency by creative.


### Lifecycle: first-time buyers aren't coming back


- **Goal:** Drive more second purchases.
- **Investigation:** The agent looks at what separates one-time buyers from repeat buyers.
- **Evidence:** Customers who buy across more than one category are much less likely to churn, and text offers have done the best job of getting people to try a second category.
- **Recommendation:** A two-message cross-sell SMS journey for at-risk first-time buyers.
- **Action:** The agent builds the audience and drafts the journey for the team to review.
- **Measurement:** Repeat purchase rate for that audience compared with a holdout group.


### Customer analytics: which customers matter most, and why


- **Goal:** Understand what drives lifetime value.
- **Investigation:** The agent breaks down LTV by segment, first product purchased, and acquisition channel.
- **Evidence:** A segment that next month's calendar barely targets has above-average LTV.
- **Recommendation:** Size the segment and plan campaigns for it.
- **Action:** Save the segment as an audience in Customer Studio.
- **Measurement:** A recurring report on that segment's growth and value.


## Why agentic CDPs matter now


Marketing teams are expected to do more without adding people. Customer journeys cross more channels and produce more data than one analyst can keep up with. Routine questions wait in the same queue as big analysis projects, and good ideas stall somewhere between "we should look into that" and a live campaign.


The models behind agents only recently got good enough to work through open-ended problems reliably, and that's what makes an agentic CDP possible now. The reason to care is practical: it cuts the time between spotting something in the data, deciding what to do about it, and getting it live.


## What to look for in an agentic CDP


If you're evaluating agentic CDPs, these questions separate real agentic capability from an AI chat box with a new label:


- **Can it rank and check its own findings?** Ask how it decides which ideas are worth showing you, and what it does with ideas the data can't support.
- **Does it work from your warehouse data?** Agents that only see one platform's data will give you partial answers.
- **Does it connect to your channels?** Campaign and creative data from ad and lifecycle platforms makes recommendations much better.
- **Does it understand marketing?** Ask how it tells seasonality from a real change, or an awareness campaign from a conversion campaign.
- **Can it act on what it finds?** Look for a direct path to audiences, journeys, and reports.
- **Does it keep people in charge?** Marketers should set the goals and approve what ships.
- **Does it remember?** Recommendations should get better as agents learn about your business.
- **Can the vendor show it working today?** Ask for a demo on your own use cases, and ask which features are generally available and which are still in beta.

We helped define the[Composable CDP](https://hightouch.com/platform/composable-cdp) , and our agentic CDP is built on that same foundation. Our agents connect directly to your data warehouse without copying data. They also connect to the ad channels and lifecycle platforms your team already uses, and to the goals and business rules you share with them.


Marketers can ask questions in plain language and get answers with charts, tables, and recommendations. Marketers review, refine, and launch, and the results feed back into the next round of recommendations.


## The future CDP helps you decide what to do next


An agentic CDP is a customer data platform that finds, ranks, and helps you act on marketing opportunities in your data. It still does everything a composable CDP does, and it adds the investigation work that used to happen outside the platform, or didn't happen at all.


You'll see the value in two places: the ideas you'd have missed, and the ideas you can skip because the agents already checked them and found nothing there. Marketers spend more time deciding and less time waiting for someone to pull the data, which is what being a[manager of agents](https://hightouch.com/blog/agentic-marketing-platform) looks like day to day.


## Frequently asked questions


**What is an agentic CDP?** An agentic CDP is a customer data platform that uses AI agents to analyze customer and campaign data, find and rank marketing opportunities, and help marketers act on them by building audiences, journeys, and reports.


**How is an agentic CDP different from a traditional CDP?** A traditional CDP stores and syncs customer data so marketers can carry out campaigns they've already planned. An agentic CDP also investigates the data, surfaces opportunities, and helps build the audiences and journeys needed to act on them.


**Is an agentic CDP the same as a composable CDP?** No. A composable CDP keeps customer data in your warehouse and builds audiences and journeys on top of it. An agentic CDP builds on that foundation by adding agents that investigate, recommend, and help carry out the work.


**Does an agentic CDP replace analysts or marketers?** No. It handles routine questions and background investigation so analysts can focus on bigger problems and marketers can spend more time on decisions. People still set the goals and approve what goes live.


**What should I look for when evaluating an agentic CDP?** Look for agents that rank and verify their findings, work from your warehouse data, connect to your ad and lifecycle channels, and lead directly into audiences, journeys, and reports. Ask the vendor to show it working on your own use cases.
